title: Tax Controversy & Litigation: A Practitioner's Guide to the IRS Process
summary: Learn to navigate IRS tax controversies from audits to litigation, including the role of 30-day and 90-day letters, Appeals, CDP hearings, and court options.
body_text: What happens when the IRS disagrees with a tax return? Tax controversy is the formal process of resolving a dispute with a taxing authority—most often, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). It begins when the IRS questions the accuracy of a return, and it can end in an administrative settlement or escalate into litigation in federal court. In Fiscal Year 2024, the IRS closed approximately 505,000 examinations, underscoring how common these disputes are. Yet for many taxpayers and professionals alike, the IRS procedural process remains opaque and intimidating. This guide breaks down each phase of a U.S. tax controversy, highlighting the strategic decisions practitioners must make at every stage. It also demonstrates how tools like TaxGPT assist with document review, audit defense, appeals strategy, and litigation preparation. While the Ultimate Guide to Tax Research explains how to identify and interpret tax law, this guide focuses on what to do when those interpretations are challenged. The First Stage — IRS Examination (Audit) What Happens During an IRS Examination? An IRS examination, more commonly referred to as an audit, is the entry point of the formal tax controversy process. This is where the IRS reviews a taxpayer’s return to verify the accuracy of the information reported. Examinations can be triggered by discrepancies in reported income, suspicious deductions or credits, or simply through random selection and algorithmic risk scoring. Depending on the complexity of the issue, an audit may be resolved quickly or it may open the door to a lengthy tax dispute that could escalate to the IRS Independent Office of Appeals or even litigation. Types of Audits: Correspondence, Office, and Field There are three main forms of IRS audits , each varying in complexity and level of taxpayer involvement: Correspondence Audit: The most common type, conducted entirely by mail or electronically. While typically limited in scope and intended for quick resolution, it can become complex, spanning multiple rounds of document requests or statute extensions. Mishandling can expand the scope or trigger escalation. Office Audit: The taxpayer (or their representative) is asked to appear at a local IRS office with specific records. These audits typically involve multiple issues or a higher risk profile. Having a prepared representative is crucial to control the narrative and avoid unnecessary expansion of the audit scope. Field Audit: The most comprehensive and intrusive form of audit. IRS agents visit the taxpayer’s place of business or residence to conduct an in-depth examination. Field audits are often reserved for high-income individuals, complex businesses, or issues involving large dollar amounts. Practitioners must carefully manage these audits to protect their client’s position and limit overreach. Pro Tip: An early and accurate framing of the taxpayer’s story (backed by documentation) can significantly reduce the risk of the audit expanding into unrelated areas. The Examiner’s Tool: Form 4564 (Information Document Request) A key procedural mechanism during audits is the Form 4564, Information Document Request (IDR). This form is how the IRS formally requests records, explanations, and data from the taxpayer. Practitioners must treat each IDR seriously and strategically: Respond completely and clearly: Incomplete or vague responses can lead to additional IDRs or broader audit scopes. Organize documentation effectively: Poor organization delays resolution and increases scrutiny. Clarify ambiguous requests: IRS examiners sometimes issue broad or unclear IDRs. It's the practitioner’s role to narrow their scope where possible. Well-managed IDR responses are a practitioner’s best defense against audit expansion and a key part of audit defense strategy. The Outcome: Understanding the 30-Day Letter At the end of the audit, the IRS may either accept the return as filed or propose adjustments. If it proposes changes, the taxpayer will receive a 30-day letter, which is generally a Letter 525 or 915. This document plays a pivotal role in the tax controversy timeline: Purpose: To inform the taxpayer of the IRS’s proposed changes and provide an opportunity to respond. Origin: It is issued only after the audit concludes with unresolved issues. Response Options: Agree with the findings and pay any tax owed. File a Formal Protest requesting a hearing with the IRS Independent Office of Appeals. Do nothing, which will result in the issuance of a Statutory Notice of Deficiency (90-day letter). Practitioners must treat the 30-day letter as a strategic fork in the road. Failing to act within the 30-day window can severely limit a taxpayer’s future rights. If the taxpayer and the examiner cannot reach an agreement, the controversy moves from the examination phase to the administrative appeals process, or straight to litigation if the taxpayer desires. The IRS Independent Office of Appeals What Is the Role of the IRS Office of Appeals? When a dispute remains unresolved after an IRS examination, the case may enter a critical second phase: administrative resolution through the IRS Independent Office of Appeals (Appeals). This office plays a unique and essential role in the tax controversy process. Established to ensure due process and reduce unnecessary litigation, Appeals is an independent function within the IRS. Its mission is to resolve tax disputes fairly and impartially, without the need to go to court. A high percentage of cases handled by Appeals are resolved without advancing to litigation, saving time, money, and resources for both the IRS and the taxpayer. Who Handles the Case? Cases are reviewed by an Appeals Officer, whose authority extends beyond mere technical application of tax law. Appeals Officers are empowered to consider the hazards of litigation. Hazards of litigation refers to the legal uncertainty that could arise if the dispute were brought before a judge. If both sides face litigation risk, Appeals may settle the case based on a probability-adjusted outcome. For example, if the IRS is only 60% confident that it would prevail in Tax Court, it may offer to settle for 60% of the proposed deficiency. This risk-based settlement framework differentiates Appeals from examination and makes it a vital forum for skilled negotiation. Initiating the Appeals Process: Filing a Formal Protest To enter this phase, a taxpayer must respond to the 30-day letter by filing a protest. The form of the protest depends on the amount in dispute. Cases involving amounts greater than $25,000 require a formal written protest. This formal protest must include: A statement of intention to appeal Detailed identification of disputed items A statement of facts and legal grounds supporting the taxpayer’s position Supporting documentation and relevant legal authorities The Appeals Conference Once the protest is accepted, an appeals conference is scheduled. This is a non-adversarial meeting between the taxpayer (or their representative) and the Appeals Officer. Key features of this stage: Less formal than court proceedings, but still highly procedural Opportunity to present evidence, clarify legal interpretations, and narrow issues Negotiation-centric, allowing for flexibility in settlement based on legal and factual analysis Appeals are not required to adopt the examiner’s position. In fact, Appeals Officers review the case independently and may disagree with the examiner if the facts or law support the taxpayer’s argument. Strategic Implications For practitioners, Appeals is often the best opportunity to resolve a tax dispute without incurring the cost, time, and uncertainty of court. It also allows for: A reset in tone from the often adversarial audit experience Introduction of new arguments or case law Application of broader judgment, including fairness and administrative efficiency Note, however, that if the taxpayer introduces new facts that were not disclosed during the audit, the Appeals Officer may return the case to IRS Examination to reopen the audit. Collection Due Process & Rapid Appeals What Are the Options for Accelerated Dispute Resolution? Not all tax disputes follow a linear path from examination to appeals to litigation. In some cases, especially when collection actions are imminent or when time is of the essence, alternative procedures offer taxpayers faster and more flexible resolution paths. Two key options are the Collection Due Process (CDP) hearing and the Rapid Appeals Process (RAP). Collection Due Process (CDP) Hearings When the IRS initiates collection actions, such as a federal tax lien or levy, the taxpayer has a statutory right to request a Collection Due Process hearing before the action is finalized. This request is made by filing Form 12153. Purpose of a CDP Hearing To challenge the appropriateness of the IRS’s collection action To propose alternative arrangements, such as: Installment agreements Offers in Compromise Currently Not Collectible status To raise issues such as innocent spouse relief, collection statute expiration, or prior bankruptcy discharges A CDP hearing pauses enforcement and gives the taxpayer a chance to negotiate or resolve issues before assets are seized. The hearing is conducted by a Settlement Officer from the IRS Office of Appeals, reinforcing the importance of this office in multiple stages of the controversy process. If the taxpayer disagrees with the outcome of the CDP hearing, they can petition the U.S. Tax Court, making it a powerful tool for both resolution and legal protection. The Rapid Appeals Process (RAP) The Rapid Appeals Process (RAP) is a pilot program developed to expedite the resolution of large-dollar disputes. It allows taxpayers to enter into early-stage mediation with the IRS Office of Appeals and IRS Examination to improve efficiency and timeliness of Appeals resolution.. Key Attributes of RAP Initiated through an agreement between the taxpayer and the IRS Involves pre-conference meetings between IRS Examination, Appeals, and the taxpayer Focuses on identifying core issues and accelerating resolution before formal escalation RAP is particularly valuable in high-stakes corporate cases where early clarity on exposure can influence broader financial or legal strategy. Choosing the Right Path Whether through CDP or RAP, these procedures give practitioners additional tools to manage tax disputes outside the traditional path. Both procedures: Preserve taxpayer rights Create opportunities for resolution before litigation Require strategic preparation, including the presentation of facts, law, and procedural compliance Tax Litigation How Does a Tax Dispute Go to Court? If a case remains unresolved after the IRS Appeals process, the final recourse is tax litigation. This phase begins when the IRS issues a Statutory Notice of Deficiency, commonly known as the 90-day letter. The Gateway to Litigation: The 90-Day Letter The Statutory Notice of Deficiency is the IRS’s legal prerequisite to tax litigation. It is issued when: The taxpayer has not agreed to the adjustments proposed during the audit or appeals process. The IRS intends to assess and collect the additional tax despite the disagreement. Key Attributes of the 90-Day Letter Function: Grants the taxpayer the right to petition the U.S. Tax Court without paying the tax first Critical deadline: The taxpayer has 90 days from the date of the letter to file a petition. If they fail to do so, the IRS may assess the tax, and the right to Tax Court is forfeited. Missing the 90-day deadline usually results in the tax becoming immediately due and payable, even if the taxpayer still disagrees with it. Choice of Forum: U.S. Tax Court and Other Federal Courts Once the 90-day letter is issued, taxpayers must decide where to litigate. The choice of forum is a significant strategic decision that depends on several factors, including the nature of the dispute, the need to pay the tax upfront, and desired legal precedent. Options: U.S. Tax Court Most common venue for tax litigation No payment required before filing Judges are tax law experts Generally more accessible for individual and small business taxpayers Petition must be filed within 90 days of the notice of deficiency U.S. District Court Requires full payment of the disputed tax Taxpayer must first file a claim for refund More formal, with broader procedural rules Often chosen when a jury trial is desired U.S. Court of Federal Claims Also requires prepayment and refund claim Often used in large-dollar cases or complex technical disputes No jury trial, but specialized jurisdiction over monetary claims against the government Each forum carries different implications for legal standards, cost, timeline, and litigation strategy. Practitioners must assess the forum best suited to their client’s financial position and legal arguments. Small Tax Case Procedure (IRC § 7463) For lower-dollar disputes, the Small Tax Case Procedure under IRC § 7463 offers a streamlined alternative within the U.S. Tax Court. Features of § 7463 Cases: Applies to disputes involving $50,000 or less per tax year Less formal procedures and expedited hearings Typically heard by a single judge with no written opinion published No right to appeal the decision While this procedure sacrifices some legal formality and precedent-setting value, it offers a cost-effective and faster route to resolution for qualifying taxpayers.

title: Governing AI agents for innovation and security inside the boundary you already trust
summary: Federal agencies can now safely deploy AI agents. See how Okta for AI Agents - Core delivers secure, FedRAMP-authorized governance for autonomous workflows.
body_text: Topics Identity Governance & Administration , AI Agents , FedRAMP , Compliance Table of Contents Share Ready to make Identity a business advantage? Sign up today. Get started Webinar: Securing federal AI innovation Learn how to comply with the new AI executive order and transition to identity-first governance without delaying AI adoption. Register now The recent Executive Order on “Promoting Advanced Artificial Intelligence Innovation and Security” makes the federal stance on AI unmistakable. The US policy is to promote AI innovation and security together, working with the private sector to modernize and harden government systems against external threats and to prioritize the cyber defense of civilian, defense, and national security systems. The order goes further, directing the Attorney General to prioritize enforcement against anyone who employs AI agents to unlawfully access data or further a crime. This order isn't theoretical; it's directing federal agencies to deploy AI agents immediately while simultaneously mandating that they secure them. For organizations caught between the pressure to innovate and the requirement to comply, this creates an urgent need for identity-first AI governance. While the executive order sets policy direction, the coming binding operational directives will establish specific implementation requirements for federal agencies, underscoring why identity governance for AI agents isn't a future concern—it's an immediate priority. The message to agencies is clear: Adopt AI aggressively, but secure it as you go. That puts identity at the center of the mission . Okta recently achieved significant compliance milestones with its agentic capabilities, bringing Okta for AI Agents - Core to FedRAMP environments . This milestone brings secure agent governance to Okta for Government High and eligible Okta for Government Moderate customers, marking a new era for federal cybersecurity. AI agents are the newest non-person entity—and the least governed Zero Trust has always insisted on one principle: It must apply to all identities. Agencies already know they need visibility into and automated governance of non-human identities (NHIs) , because that is a well-understood security gap. AI agents are the fastest-growing class of NHI yet, and the hardest to see. Anyone can spin one up, agents can create more agents, and each connects across apps, APIs, software as a service (SaaS) tools, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and data systems. For organizations under the new mandate to harden systems and defend against AI-enabled criminal access, an unmanaged agent is not just an operational gap—it is an unguarded door. The gap is real—and specific Government agencies are under pressure to deploy AI agents now. But running AI agents on regulated data outside a FedRAMP-authorized environment is more than just a compliance gap—it’s a significant security threat. That gap comes with concrete risks: Compliance violations: This occurs when AI agents touch data from environments that aren't FedRAMP-authorized. The moment an agent reaches regulated data outside an authorized boundary, the organization is exposed. Compounding breach risk: This happens when ungoverned agents operate at machine speed across apps, APIs, SaaS tools, and data systems with no consistent security controls. A single compromised credential doesn't grant access to one system; it grants access to everything an agent can reach before a human can intervene. Failed audits: This is common when agents run as orphaned accounts with no unique identity, no human owner, and no evidence trail. Stalled AI adoption: This occurs when the only "compliant" option is to delay deployment, putting agencies at odds with an executive order that calls for promoting innovation. Leaders are left with an impossible trade-off: Move fast and risk a violation or breach, or stay compliant by putting AI initiatives on hold. The executive order asks for both speed and security, and identity is how agencies deliver them together. Same federal boundary, new identity class Our newly launched Okta for AI Agents - Core offering closes the gap by managing the full agent lifecycle inside the same FedRAMP environments you already trust Okta to run for human identity. Same boundary. Same assurances. New coverage for a new identity class. This builds on the milestones Okta has already achieved in the federal market. Okta Identity Governance became FedRAMP High authorized earlier this year, extending modern governance and identity and access management (IAM) to federal government agencies. Bringing agents into that same identity fabric is the natural next step, not a parallel system to build and defend. To achieve this, we’ve built a blueprint for the secure agentic enterprise that leverages your existing infrastructure and sets out to answer three key questions that any agentic organization must be able to answer: Where are my agents? What can they connect to? And what can they do? 1. Discover and onboard: Where are my agents? You can't govern what you can't see, but you are accountable for your agents' actions. Every agent becomes a known, owned, first-class identity inside your environment, whether it came from a third-party platform or your own developers. To achieve this, Okta for AI Agents delivers two primary onboarding capabilities designed to bring both third-party and custom-built agents under a single, unified control plane: AI agent import: Import known agents from leading third-party platforms using pre-built integrations within the Okta Integration Network (OIN) , reducing manual setup and accelerating onboarding. AI agent registry: Bring custom-built, homegrown agents into Universal Directory as first-class identities. Assign human owners, apply the identity controls you already use, and manage every agent from one source of truth. Each agent is onboarded with a clear human owner assigned—the accountability foundation auditors expect—with an emphasis on hardened, defensible systems. 2. Protect: What can they connect to? Once agents are known and owned, you control exactly what they can reach. Admins define which resources an agent can access, how it authenticates, and what permissions it receives, with runtime enforcement on every connection. This replaces long-lived static keys and standing access with scoped, short-lived credentials issued only for what the agent needs. Protection extends across a variety of resource types: Authorization servers: Set up defined and enforced access for homegrown agents. Applications: Connect through brokered consent for secure, user-authorized access to third-party apps, enforced at runtime. MCP servers: Connect directly as managed resources with admin-defined controls and runtime enforcement. The principle is least privilege, applied consistently, which is also the most direct defense against the over-scoped or hijacked agent the order is concerned with. 3. Govern: What can they do? Agents enter the same governance lifecycle you already use for your workforce, so oversight is continuous rather than a one-time setup. This mirrors the modern identity governance and administration capabilities federal agencies already rely on: Streamlined, context-aware certifications to defend against privilege creep, and a complete audit trail for every access decision. To enforce this continuous oversight, Okta for AI Agents extends our core governance capabilities to autonomous workflows through these key features: User Access Requests for AI Agents: Users request access from their dashboard while admins manage approvals, automate actions, and enforce time-bound permissions. User Access Certifications for AI Agents: Agents use the same standardized certification workflows as SaaS apps, so owners, managers, and security admins can review, approve, or revoke access with full auditability and automatic enforcement. Agent deactivation: When an agent deviates from its intended mission or accesses sensitive data unexpectedly, security teams have a real-time kill switch to contain the risk before it escalates into a larger incident. Audit logs and telemetry: Log all agent activity, including tool calls, authorization decisions, and access attempts, and optionally stream it to your security information and event management (SIEM) platform, providing the complete audit trail that fulfills the rigorous reporting requirements of oversight bodies like the Government Accountability Office (GAO). What this means for federal agencies Identity security isn't a compliance checkbox; it's the foundational layer that enables safe AI adoption. As our CEO, Todd McKinnon, notes, "You can't move fast on AI unless you can do it securely." The executive order recognizes this. Now organizations need to act on it. Innovate aggressively. Secure relentlessly. You don't have to choose between the speed of AI adoption and the strength of your security posture. title: Built to Work: Inside Utilimaster’s Kansas City Upfit Center
body_text: At the core is a commitment to a practical, field-tested approach built around how professionals use their vehicles every day, delivering upfits that improve workflow, boost productivity, enhance safety, and drive profitability. With a history of upfitting more than 12,000 vehicles in a year in Kansas City and direct OEM ship-thru partnerships, Utilimaster ensures vehicles are completed efficiently and correctly the first time. “Customers don’t have time to manage multiple vendors or chase down delays,” says Nick Troiola, Director of Sales for Utilimaster. “Our Kansas City Upfit Center is designed to remove that friction, bringing everything under one roof so vehicles are built right, delivered faster, and ready to perform the moment they hit the road.” Smart Packages. Custom Solutions. No two businesses operate exactly the same. This is why Utilimaster’s Kansas City Upfit Center offers both pre-configured packages and fully customized solutions tailored to specific industries and operational needs. Inside Utilimaster’s Kansas City Upfit Center, vehicles move through a streamlined process designed to deliver efficient, fully equipped, job-ready builds under one roof. Building Hard Working Contractor Packages For HVAC technicians, plumbers, electricians, and service professionals, time and organization are everything. Utilimaster’s contractor packages are built with these demands in mind, offering optimized layouts, professional-grade storage, and durable, field-tested components. These packages are designed for efficiency from the start, with quick installation and fast turnaround times that keep your business moving. Whether you manage one vehicle or an expanding fleet, you get a reliable, ready-to-work solution without unnecessary delays. Supporting Public Works and Municipalities Fleets Utilimaster also brings its expertise to public sector operations. From small-town departments to large municipal fleets, the Kansas City Upfit Center delivers dependable solutions tailored to public works teams, service crews, and rural communities. What sets Utilimaster apart is its ability to scale service without compromising quality. Smaller municipalities receive the same high-level equipment, attention, and turnaround times trusted by major cities, ensuring every community has access to reliable, work-ready vehicles. Pickup Upfits Built on Real-World Experience Pickup trucks are essential across countless industries, and Utilimaster has refined its approach through millions of miles of real-world ride-alongs. The result is a lineup of 36 curated pickup upfit packages designed to enhance organization, safety, and productivity. These packages offer a fast, effective way to get vehicles job-ready, whether they’re used for service calls, deliveries, or skilled trades. And when off-the-shelf solutions aren’t enough, custom configurations ensure every vehicle meets exact operational requirements from day one. The KC production facility offers 36 pickup upfit packages to improve organization, safety, and productivity, with custom options so your vehicle can get the job done on day one. Interior Upfits From durable flooring and bulkhead partitions to shelving systems, racks, bins, and drawers, every interior component is designed to maximize space and efficiency. Add-ons like laptop mounts, keyless entry, and upgraded lighting further enhance functionality. Safety & Technology Safety is never optional. Camera systems, safety equipment, cab racks, and trailer tow systems help protect both drivers and equipment while improving operational confidence. Climate & Crew Configurations Whether you need advanced HVAC systems or crew cab setups, Utilimaster ensures vehicles remain comfortable and functional in any working environment. Pickup & Exterior Solutions Exterior upgrades such as toolboxes, ladder racks, headache racks, bed slides, and lighting systems turn pickups into fully capable mobile workstations. Faster Turnaround with Ship-Thru Capabilities One of the biggest advantages of working with Utilimaster is its direct OEM ship-thru partnerships. Vehicles can be sent straight from manufacturers to the Kansas City facility for upfitting, reducing handling time and accelerating deployment. Supported platforms span a full range of commercial vehicles, from cargo vans to electric delivery models and heavy-duty pickups, giving fleets the flexibility to operate across virtually any industry. Skilled technicians upfit a vehicle with precision, transforming it into a safe, organized, work-ready solution as it comes off the line. One Partner. Total Confidence. At the end of the day, the Utilimaster Kansas City Upfit Center is built around one simple idea: Make it easier for businesses to get the vehicles they need, ready to perform from day one. With smart, complete packages, custom solutions, and a proven design philosophy, it’s a partner that helps you stay focused on the work ahead, while they handle everything behind the scenes. “Our customers depend on vehicles that are ready to perform the moment they’re delivered,” says Jacob Farmer President of Commercial & Fleet at Aebi Schmidt Group. “By investing in integrated upfit capabilities and streamlined processes, we’re helping fleets reduce downtime, improve productivity, and scale with confidence.”

title: System Update: Take Control of Your Money with Coinbase
summary: Today, we’re launching several new products that further our mission of creating the Everything Exchange and being the most intelligent financial services app in the world.
body_text: Since our last System Update, we have been hard at work building upon the product foundations that make the Everything Exchange possible. More assets to trade, more ways to trade them, and a more robust financial suite that enables you to take full control of your money in one place. Today, we are launching even more new features and services that expand on each of these three pillars. Coinbase is building the future of finance, where you can manage your money with just one interface, and one login. We’re saying “no” to financial fragmentation, and the new products we’re introducing today take us several steps closer to that future. Trade more on Coinbase We are dramatically expanding what you can trade – and how you trade – on Coinbase, bringing every type of asset and market under one roof. For years we’ve laid the groundwork, and now we’re bringing the benefits of crypto to stock trading. Next month, we will introduce tokenized stocks for our non-U.S. customers.¹ Backed 1:1 by the underlying asset, Coinbase tokenized stocks will represent true equity ownership, including dividend payouts and complete shareholder rights, alongside the programmatic utility of the onchain economy. For the first time, you can trade U.S.-based stocks 24/7, lend your shares to earn yield, use them as collateral for a loan, or even gift them directly to someone else as easily as sending a text message. In the coming months, we’ll also be rolling out options trading for crypto and stocks , directly on Coinbase.² This unlocks a new level of sophistication for trading strategies on Coinbase with a full range of motion in both your traditional and digital assets. On the equities front, you can now transfer your existing stock portfolios from other platforms directly to Coinbase, and trade nearly every major stock, index, and ETF you can think of in the U.S. And now, traders can complement their crypto portfolio with access to equities on Coinbase Advanced . This includes benefits like zero commission fees, TradingView charting (e.g. indicators), fractional shares and up to 3.5% rewards on trade-ready USDC balances.³ Beyond traditional public equities, we are introducing real world asset (RWA) perpetual futures , granting targeted exposure to thematic equity indices like AI, China, Defense, and the Tech 100. Introduced earlier this month, our new Pre-IPO perps also offer early exposure to high-interest companies before they hit public exchanges, starting with SpaceX plus Anthropic and OpenAI coming soon.⁴ Since launching prediction markets access earlier this year, we’ve seen incredible demand.² And we’re now bringing you more contracts with even faster and richer trading experiences. Today, we’re introducing: Crypto binaries: Trade time-boxed “up or down” markets on assets like BTC, ETH, SOL and more. This allows you to trade predictions on outcomes across 15-minute, hourly, daily, monthly, and annual intervals. Combos: Bundle multiple predictions into a single trade, across any category on the platform. That means combining trades on economic indicators alongside global political events, or tapping into your read on sports game outcomes and player performance all in a single position. On the onchain frontier, we’re making your path to DEX trading even more direct with more tokens and faster access. Tomorrow, you will be able to trade any of the tens of millions of Base or Solana tokens the instant they become available onchain with our New Launches tab in the Coinbase app.⁵ We’re also giving Coinbase Advanced a major upgrade . Modular, institutional-grade, and built for cross-asset execution, we redesigned our sophisticated trading platform to meet you where you are. Your strategy, your set up, your stocks and crypto side-by-side on a single interface. Just choose a template or drag and drop widgets to build a custom trading layout that meets your needs. And in the next few months we are bringing together our U.S. spot exchange, international derivatives exchanges, and Deribit into a unified, regulated global liquidity pool to give customers the most liquid spot, perpetuals, and options access in the world. And we are giving everyone access – Coinbase is the first approved by the CFTC to offer global regulated crypto derivatives, including options, to Americans. Trade smarter with Coinbase With the broadest range of assets available in the market, there's even more opportunity if you know what you're looking for. So we are delivering the tooling required for intelligent trading in a global, cross-asset marketplace. Today, we’re launching Coinbase Advisor – rolling out first to Coinbase One members in the U.S. It’s one of the world’s first AI-powered, SEC-registered in-app investment advisors designed to bring professional-grade investment advice to everyone. From helping you design complex tax-loss harvesting to turning breaking news into multi-asset trade recommendations, it handles the heavy analytical lifting so you can optimize your wealth-building strategies with ease. Access to professional grade investment advice now sits in the Coinbase app, available 24/7 without the traditional cost barriers.⁶ For those looking to dive even deeper, we’re making Coinbase the most powerful platform for agentic trading with Coinbase for Agents. Now you can enable any AI agent to execute sophisticated strategies on your portfolio around the clock. Using natural language, you can define your agent's exact tasks and boundaries, whether assigning it to execute a market thesis across spot and derivatives or utilizing the x402 protocol to pay for premium, paywalled financial research. You can confine your agent to an isolated sub-account and set precise limits around capital allocation, asset permissions, and trade sizes – ensuring you grant it a clearly defined budget and trading parameters.⁷ Your primary financial platform On Coinbase, your money never sits still. It earns when you spend it. It stays in the market, even when you need cash. And it grows the moment your paycheck lands. We continue to evolve our financial services products to work even harder for you, providing flexible, capital-efficient alternatives to legacy banking constraints. We are expanding the utility of the Coinbase One Card today with the launch of the first travel platform that gives you 5% Bitcoin back on every booking, sent straight to your account. The new Travel Portal eliminates the stress of expiring or devaluing traditional loyalty points. No games, just Bitcoin – with access to all the travel protections and benefits offered through the American Express Network. This is the first of many boosted rewards for cardholders coming this year.⁸ We want the Coinbase One Card to be available to everyone, no matter your credit history. Today, we're introducing USDC-backed access to the Coinbase One Card , built for everyone who is overlooked by traditional credit bureaus. This update allows users who aren't approved for a traditional line of credit to secure a Coinbase One Card using USDC as collateral. So you can unlock Bitcoin rewards on everyday purchases while continuing to earn rewards on the underlying USDC deposit, paid out every single week. All while being able to help build your credit with every on-time payment.⁹ With so many ways to earn and use your crypto, staking your assets shouldn’t mean they stay locked up. Starting today, you can borrow against your staked Solana on Coinbase, powered by JitoSOL, via our ongoing integration with Morpho on Base. In addition to borrowing against BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, DOGE, ADA, and LTC, you can now unlock liquidity from more of your yield-generating assets: cbETH (up to $1mn) and now JitoSOL (up to $100k).¹⁰ Making Coinbase the ultimate hub for managing your entire financial life means you need comprehensive security controls over all your outgoing funds. So we’ve begun rolling out Transfer Protection – a new defensive framework including time-delayed withdrawals, providing a vital review window to verify transactions before they execute, alongside customizable daily limits that prevent unauthorized, large-scale outflows. You can also implement multi-party approval workflows, creating a collaborative authentication process for outbound money movement. These rigorous guardrails ensure that as you store, save, and grow your wealth on Coinbase, it remains entirely under your command. Coinbase infrastructure for your business Coinbase has spent nearly 15 years building crypto infrastructure at scale to power our own products, and today our all-new Coinbase Developer Platform (CDP) makes it simple for any company to participate in the onchain economy. One access point unlocks access to our wallet infrastructure, payments capabilities, trading systems, and stablecoin issuance. Where we're really seeing crypto use cases take off is around stablecoin payments, with nearly a trillion dollars in stablecoin volume last year on Coinbase products alone. That’s where Coinbase Payments comes in – it’s a complete stablecoin payments solution within CDP built on USDC, Base, institutional-grade custody, and a powerful API layer. Companies like Checkout.com are already using it to move money faster, cheaper, and more globally than ever before. For businesses that want to offer crypto to their customers without the complexity of licensing, we're announcing a fully custodial infrastructure solution , powered by 80 global regulatory licenses and our stress-tested compliance infrastructure. We’re launching with partners like Klarna and Webull to bring launch timelines down from years to weeks. CDP is also built for the agentic economy. We’re partnering with AWS to unlock native agent payments on AWS AgentCore . And Coinbase Payments APIs are now agentic-enabled out of the box . That means companies like OpenRouter – the largest AI model exchange and a Coinbase Payments customer – will be able to accept payments seamlessly from both humans and agents. The future of finance won’t be split between a bank, a brokerage, and a crypto wallet. It is unified, intelligent, onchain, and on Coinbase. Explore all these new features today.
